records.question: According to R. T. Chamberlin's observations quoted in the section, how far below sea level does the broad wave-cut platform around Tutuila now lie?
records.ground_truth_answer: This broad shelf "now lies at least (though probably not much more than) 400 feet below sealevel."
ground_truth_chunks: The island of Tutuila is a volcanic pile whose slopes have been attacked by the sea until a broad wave-cut platform, 2 miles in width, has come to surround the island.
This broad shelf of planation, originally cut in the volcanic rocks not far below the sea level, now lies at least (though probably not much more than) 400 feet below sealevel...
